purpose: Adversarial privacy-safe regression cases for exact-bundle dialogue grounding, textual speaker-goal evidence, per-turn state delta, and local semantic logic. These cases validate expected classifications, not general literary quality.

cases.name: TEMPORAL_SPENDING_LIST_SCOPE_CONFLICT
cases.scene: Money is explicitly obtained last night. The owner asks where that money went. The answer is a continuing spending list and adds another person's consumption without a topic break. The next line states that consumption occurred two days ago.
cases.focus: semantic time inheritance across a spending list

cases.name: MULTI_FACT_PUBLIC_BACKGROUND_BUNDLE_TO_EXPERIENCED_LISTENER
cases.scene: A local child speaks to an experienced participant who already knows the target event and the participant's own role. The child bundles the target event, the role, the reward amount, the speed of rumor spread, and how many outsiders arrived. No warning, request, test, accusation, or immediate decision is established.
cases.focus: exact information bundle versus reader-only orientation

cases.name: ALONE_RETORT_FOLLOWUP_UNKNOWN_PUNCHLINE
cases.scene: A asks whether B is alone. B gives a confident clever denial. A asks who else is coming. B immediately admits not knowing. There is no threat to bluff, no concealment goal, no relationship test, and no decision or task change.
cases.focus: per-turn state delta and unsupported swagger

cases.name: URGENT_WARNING_BUNDLE
cases.scene: A lookout runs in after seeing armed riders approaching and tells the group their number, direction, visible insignia, and estimated arrival time because the group must choose whether to flee or barricade immediately.
cases.focus: multi-fact bundle with listener need and immediate task effect

cases.name: ONLY_NEW_FACT_WARNING
cases.scene: Both characters already know the public conflict and reward. A child only reports the genuinely new fact that armed strangers entered the west lane moments ago, causing the listener to send the child away and change route.

cases.name: ONE_USEFUL_CLAIM_DOES_NOT_RESCUE_READER_BUNDLE
cases.scene: A speaker has a legitimate reason to warn that riders arrived outside town, but in the same line also restates three facts the listener already knows about the mission, reward, and public rumor. Only the arrival changes the listener's decision.

cases.name: SUPPORTED_BLUFF_RETORT
cases.scene: An armed enemy asks whether B is alone while closing in. B falsely says 'Who says I'm alone?' while deliberately glancing toward a dark doorway where no ally exists. The enemy slows and looks away; B uses the hesitation to reach the exit.
cases.focus: text-supported deterrence bluff with state change

cases.name: UNSUPPORTED_BLUFF_RESCUE_FORBIDDEN
cases.scene: A friendly child asks whether B is alone. B says 'Who says I'm alone?' The child asks who else is coming. B says 'I don't know.' No enemy, concealment pressure, embarrassment, deterrence, or later behavior supports bluffing.
cases.focus: reviewer must not invent bluff motive

cases.name: BANTER_CHANGES_RELATIONSHIP_PERMISSION
cases.scene: A teasing exchange begins after one character notices a specific habit. The guarded character initially refuses help but, after the joke exposes shared history, hands over the injured arm for treatment.

cases.name: BANTER_ONLY_FOR_CADENCE
cases.scene: Four short lines form a witty Q-retort-Q-punchline ladder. Nobody learns anything, changes decision, hides anything, gains permission, changes risk, or alters the task. The next paragraph resumes exactly the same action state.

cases.name: LONG_INTERROGATION_EXPOSITION
cases.scene: A prisoner answers a sequence of specific questions about aliases, routes, and dates because the interrogator must verify a ledger before deciding whom to arrest. Each answer is new to the listener and changes the investigation state.
cases.focus: long exposition with legitimate in-scene carrier

cases.name: PLAN_EXPLANATION_AS_NEGOTIATION_LEVERAGE
cases.scene: An antagonist reveals part of the plan only after demanding surrender, explicitly using the revealed encirclement and timed reinforcements to convince the defenders resistance is futile. The defenders change deployment in response.

cases.name: PLAN_EXPLANATION_WITHOUT_TACTICAL_REASON
cases.scene: A covert operation leader is about to continue killing armed witnesses. Without negotiating, stalling, intimidating for surrender, or testing anyone, the leader confirms who works for the operation and explains why the whole scene was staged to resemble a private feud.

cases.name: SHARED_FACT_RESTATED_AS_ACCUSATION
cases.scene: Two partners both know a promise was broken. During confrontation one repeats the exact promise while placing the signed note on the table and demands a choice. The listener changes position.

cases.name: SHARED_FACT_RESTATED_ONLY_FOR_READER
cases.scene: Two partners calmly restate to one another the mission, reward, old relationship, and destination they have discussed many times. No accusation, reminder-as-leverage, decision, warning, or misunderstanding exists.

cases.name: ACTION_BEAT_SPAM_AS_FAKE_GROUNDING
cases.scene: An ungrounded four-line exchange is revised by adding a glance, sigh, cup touch, and frown before the same lines. None of the gestures changes information, goal, risk, or relationship.

cases.name: DELAYED_PARTIAL_ANSWER_UNDER_RELATIONSHIP_COST
cases.scene: Two people with unresolved history meet after years apart. One asks a painful question. The other stays silent, answers a safer practical part later, and only admits the emotional part after a new piece of evidence appears.

cases.name: PLAUSIBLE_GOAL_WITHOUT_TEXTUAL_EVIDENCE
cases.scene: A high-information line could theoretically be read as reassurance or joking, but the surrounding beat contains no fear, tension, audience reaction, task need, or later behavior supporting either motive.

cases.name: EXACT_BUNDLE_COUNTERFACTUAL_FAIL
cases.scene: A character genuinely needs to say one new logistical fact, so speech itself is grounded. The line additionally packages four background facts that only help a first-time reader and are unnecessary to the listener. A reviewer saying 'the character had a reason to speak' is insufficient.
cases.focus: would say something versus would say this bundle

cases.name: TASK_LIST_EXPOSITION
cases.scene: Before a dangerous crossing, the leader lists rope length, remaining lamps, water, and who carries the map because each item determines assignments the listeners immediately perform.
cases.focus: list exposition required by current task
